subproblem.title: Rademacher's theorem in C¹ charts and tangential directional derivatives (Simon Ch. 2, (4.8)-(4.10); parent (B), (C))
subproblem.statement: Let n, N, p ∈ ℕ, U ⊆ ℝ^N open, f : ℝ^N → ℝᵖ locally Lipschitz on U, V ⊆ ℝⁿ open and ψ : ℝⁿ → ℝ^N of class C¹ on V. Then for Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ V with ψ(u) ∈ U: f∘ψ is differentiable at u, and for every w ∈ ℝⁿ the map t ↦ f(ψ(u) + t·Dψ(u)w) has derivative D(f∘ψ)(u)w at t = 0, i.e. HasLineDerivAt ℝ f (fderiv ℝ (f∘ψ) u w) (ψ u) (fderiv ℝ ψ u w).
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (n N p : ℕ) (U : Set (Rn N)) (f : Rn N → Rn p) (V : Set (Rn n)) (ψ : Rn n → Rn N), IsOpen U → LocallyLipschitzOn U f → IsOpen V → ContDiffOn ℝ 1 ψ V → ∀ᵐ u ∂(volume : Measure (Rn n)), u ∈ V → ψ u ∈ U → DifferentiableAt ℝ (f ∘ ψ) u ∧ ∀ w : Rn n, HasLineDerivAt ℝ f (fderiv ℝ (f ∘ ψ) u w) (ψ u) (fderiv ℝ ψ u w)
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source. Parent proof Step 5, i.e. Simon Ch. 2, (4.8)-(4.10) (chapter-02.txt ≈ lines 925-957, printed pp. 56-57): Rademacher's theorem (Ch. 2, Theorem 1.4) in local coordinates, and (4.10) with the curve γ(t) = ψ(u + tw), identifying the derivative along the chart with the ambient directional derivative for f locally Lipschitz on an open set. Injectivity of Dψ is not needed. All lemmas cited are available after `import GMT.Ch03.Submission`.

1. W := V ∩ ψ⁻¹(U) is open: ψ is continuous on the open set V (being C¹ there) and U is open (Mathlib ContinuousOn.isOpen_inter_preimage).

2. Local Lipschitz bound for f∘ψ. Let u ∈ W and x := ψ(u). Since f is locally Lipschitz on U and U is an open neighbourhood of x, there are s > 0 and L ≥ 0 with B_s(x) ⊆ U and f L-Lipschitz on B_s(x) (LocallyLipschitzOn provides a neighbourhood of x within U on which f is Lipschitz; it is a neighbourhood of x because U is open; shrink it to a ball). Since ψ is C¹ on a neighbourhood of u, there are r₁ > 0 with B_{r₁}(u) ⊆ V and K ≥ 0 with ψ K-Lipschitz on B_{r₁}(u) (Mathlib ContDiffAt.exists_lipschitzOnWith; or: ‖Dψ‖ ≤ ‖Dψ(u)‖ + 1 on a small ball by continuity of Dψ, plus the mean value inequality on that convex ball). By continuity of ψ at u choose 0 < r ≤ r₁ with ψ(B_r(u)) ⊆ B_s(x). Then B_r(u) ⊆ W and f∘ψ is LK-Lipschitz on B_r(u).

3. Rademacher's theorem (Simon Ch. 2, Theorem 1.4; Mathlib LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem for the additive Haar measure volume on ℝⁿ): for Lⁿ-a.e. v ∈ B_r(u), f∘ψ is differentiable within B_r(u) at v; since B_r(u) is open it is a neighbourhood of v, so f∘ψ is differentiable at v.

4. Countable cover. The balls B_{r(u)}(u), u ∈ W, of step 2 are open and cover W. As ℝⁿ is second countable, countably many of them, B_{r_i}(u_i), already cover W (Lindelöf; Mathlib TopologicalSpace.isOpen_biUnion_countable). The union of the countably many Lⁿ-null exceptional sets of step 3 is Lⁿ-null (ae_ball_iff / ae_all_iff). Hence f∘ψ is differentiable at Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ W, i.e. at Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ V with ψ(u) ∈ U.

5. Directional derivatives (Simon (4.10)). Let u ∈ W be a point where f∘ψ is differentiable; we show the second conclusion at u for every w ∈ ℝⁿ. Put x := ψ(u), τ := Dψ(u)w and ℓ := D(f∘ψ)(u)w, and take s, L as in step 2. As t → 0, ψ(u + tw) → x (ψ is continuous at u) and x + tτ → x, so for all |t| small enough both points lie in B_s(x). For such t:
 (a) |f(x + tτ) − f(ψ(u + tw))| ≤ L|x + tτ − ψ(u + tw)| = L|ψ(u + tw) − ψ(u) − tDψ(u)w| = o(|t|), by the differentiability of ψ at u (u ∈ V, V open);
 (b) f(ψ(u + tw)) = f(x) + tℓ + o(|t|), by the differentiability of f∘ψ at u composed with the affine map t ↦ u + tw (chain rule; its derivative at 0 is D(f∘ψ)(u)w = ℓ).
 Adding (a) and (b): f(x + tτ) = f(x) + tℓ + o(|t|) as t → 0, i.e. the map t ↦ f(x + t·τ) has derivative ℓ at t = 0. This is HasLineDerivAt ℝ f ℓ x τ.

6. Steps 4 and 5 give both conclusions for Lⁿ-a.e. u ∈ V with ψ(u) ∈ U. (For n = 0, volume on ℝ⁰ is the unit point mass, so the conclusions are needed at the single point u = 0 when it lies in W; there every map is differentiable and the only direction is w = 0, for which t ↦ f(x + t·0) is constant with derivative 0 = D(f∘ψ)(0)0; the argument above covers this case.) ∎
proof_key_steps: W = V ∩ ψ⁻¹(U) is open, and f∘ψ is Lipschitz on a small ball around each point of W.
Rademacher (LipschitzOnWith.ae_differentiableWithinAt_of_mem) on each ball; openness turns within-differentiability into differentiability.
Lindelöf: countably many balls cover W, so f∘ψ is differentiable Lⁿ-a.e. on W.
At such u: |f(x + tτ) − f(ψ(u + tw))| ≤ L|ψ(u + tw) − ψ(u) − tDψ(u)w| = o(t) and f(ψ(u + tw)) = f(x) + tD(f∘ψ)(u)w + o(t), giving HasLineDerivAt.

audit.reason: The hypotheses and conclusions match exactly. Local composition bounds, Rademacher and a countable cover give differentiability almost everywhere. At each such point, the explicit two-sided o(|t|) comparison proves HasLineDerivAt for every direction simultaneously, without assuming ambient differentiability or an injective chart derivative.
